1.8.rationale: In the Indonesian source, the regulation’s substantive scope of “tindak kekerasan” includes physical, psychological, sexual violence, neglect, exploitation, and other violence (Pasal 7–13). It does NOT explicitly define or mention “perdagangan orang” (human trafficking) as a form of violence/abuse covered. The only place trafficking appears is in the legal basis list (“Mengingat” point 11: UU No. 21 Tahun 2007 tentang Pemberantasan Tindak Pidana Perdagangan Orang). Citing a referenced statute in the preamble does not, by itself, mean the policy’s scope includes trafficking as an indicator item. The judge incorrectly treated a legal citation as substantive inclusion, so this is a reasoning/threshold error rather than a retrieval or translation problem.

4.2.evaluator_rationale: While the policy mentions education and socialization about the rights of women and children and defines gender equality in an explanatory section, the provided sentences do not show primary prevention activities explicitly focused on gender equality and/or women’s rights (as distinct from rights/protection in the context of violence).

REGIONAL REGULATION OF KEPAHIANG REGENCY

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their innate nature (fitrah) and their God-given nature/role (kodrat) without discrimination.

Sociologically, acts of violence against women and children have been increasingly rising both in quantity and quality. This is in line with technological developments that can be emulated at any time by perpetrators of acts of violence, thus also increasing in quality. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who mostly work and live on plantations have neglected their attention and responsibility toward their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a regional regulation.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

4.2.rationale: The Indonesian text contains explicit primary-prevention education/socialization measures about rights: Pasal 14 ayat (2) huruf (e) requires “melakukan sosialisasi tentang peraturan perundang-undangan yang berkaitan dengan hak-hak dan perlindungan perempuan dan anak terhadap tindak kekerasan,” and huruf (f) requires “memberikan pendidikan kritis tentang hak-hak perempuan dan anak kepada masyarakat.” This is an education activity aimed at women’s/children’s rights as prevention. Additionally, the elucidation of Pasal 2 defines “kesetaraan gender” (gender equality) and the principles include “keadilan dan kesetaraan” and “non diskriminasi.” The retrieved candidates already included Pasal 14(2)(f) and the Pasal 2 elucidation, so the judge had sufficient evidence but applied an overly narrow interpretation (demanding explicit ‘gender equality education’ wording rather than rights/gender-equality content).

6.8.evaluator_rationale: The policy includes services for women (and children) as victims as well as reporters and witnesses, and it provides legal and accompaniment services during police/prosecutor/court processes, indicating explicit support for women involved in legal proceedings at least as witnesses/reporters/victims.

ELUCIDATION OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF KEPAHIANG REGENCY
NUMBER 10 OF 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their innate nature (fitrah) and their God-given nature/role (kodrat) without discrimination.

Sociologically, acts of violence against women and children have been increasingly rising both in quantity and quality. This is in line with technological developments that can be emulated at any time by perpetrators of acts of violence, thus also increasing in quality. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who mostly work and live on plantations have neglected their attention and responsibility toward their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a regional regulation.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

6.8.rationale: The Indonesian regulation explicitly provides support for women/children in legal processes. Pasal 3 huruf (d) states services are provided to women and children not only as victims but also as “pelapor, dan saksi.” Pasal 5 huruf (g) grants “hak atas pendampingan dan bantuan hukum,” and huruf (h) grants “hak untuk mendapatkan kemudahan dalam proses peradilan.” Operationally, Pasal 19 huruf (c)-(d) mandates accompaniment and monitoring during examinations at police/prosecutor/court, and Pasal 22 huruf (b) mandates accompanying victims at investigation, prosecution, and court examination. These provisions clearly cover women involved in legal proceedings (as victims/reporters/witnesses). Since this content is in the original text and was also present in retrieved passages, the judge’s ‘Yes’ is correct and the golden label ‘No’ appears to be wrong.
